summary: David B. Gray is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe. He served as a postdoctoral fellow at Rice University and Associate Professor at Santa Clara University (attested 2008–2017).

David Brown (1762–1812) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who founded the Calcutta Auxiliary Bible Society. He studied under Joseph Milner and at Magdalene College, Cambridge, later serving as provost at Fort William College in 1800.

David Bubna-Litic works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned his PhD at Western Sydney University (attested 2000) and was a lecturer in strategic management and responsible business at the University of Technology Sydney (attested 2000).

David Burton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997). By 2010, he served as Senior Lecturer in Theology and Religious Studies at Canterbury Christ Church University.

David Dean Shulman (1949–) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his B.A. at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Ph.D. at the University of London under John Ralston Marr, later holding posts at Hebrew University and the Israel Institute for Advanced Studies.

David Drewes specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Karen C. Lang. He held teaching posts at Virginia and Indiana University, and became Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Manitoba (attested 2009–2010).

David E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of California, Los Angeles. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, UIUC, and the University of Hawaiʻi, later holding research posts at Nichibunken and Oberlin College.

David Edward Cooper (1942–) is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St Edmund Hall. He lectured at the University of Oxford (1967), served as Professor of Philosophy at Durham University (1986–2008), and was a visiting professor at Peking University (2022).

David Fiordalis is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Carleton College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan (Ph.D. under Luis O. Gómez), later serving as associate professor and department chair at Linfield University (attested 2017).
David Forbes held academic appointments at Brooklyn College and as affiliate faculty at the Graduate Center, CUNY, both attested in 2016.

David Friedman (1903–1984) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS and Professor at the University of London from circa 1950 to 1970.

David Gellner (1957–) is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. Attested at the University of Oxford beginning in 1988, he became Emeritus Professor of Social Anthropology at Oxford and Wolfson College (attested 2026).

David Germano is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992. He joined the faculty at the University of Virginia, serving as Associate Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies (attested 2000–2008).
David Gonsalez is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who pursued traditional studies under Gen Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Gordon White (1953–) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. circa 1988). He held faculty posts at the University of Virginia and UC Santa Barbara.

David Graeber (1961–2020) studied at SUNY Purchase and the University of Chicago under Marshall Sahlins. He held academic posts at Yale University (1998–2007), Goldsmiths, University of London (2007–2013), and the London School of Economics (circa 2013–2020).

David Higgins is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held an appointment at the University of Vienna (attested 2015) and serves as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

David J. Kalupahana (1936–2014) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. Educated at the University of Ceylon and SOAS University of London (PhD under Stanley Weinstein and David Friedman), he taught at Ceylon before becoming Philosophy Department Chairman at the University of Hawaiʻi in 1972.

David Jones is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Hawaiʻi. Attested in 2007, he served as a professor of philosophy in the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

David K. Wyatt (1937–2006) was a historian who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell University (Ph.D. circa 1966). He taught at SOAS and Michigan before serving as History Department Chair at Cornell (1969–2002) and AAS president (1993).
